12.53pm So West Indies are bowled out for 243, in what is a fighting total but probably 
under par considering the favourable batting conditions. But that they have even that 
much is down to Keacy Carty's 96-ball 87, though that too might not have been, had a 
straightforward chance been taken when he was on 8. But he made his second-chance 
count, stringing together stands of 41, 32, 63 and 25 after West Indies had found 
themselves at first 81 for 5, and then 123 for 7. Sri Lanka would drop three chances in 
total, but it was an otherwise consummate outing in the field. Maheesh Theekshana 
was once more the star, picking up yet another 4-for to cripple the West Indies batting 
line-up after Johnson Charles (39) had got them off to a flyer. Each of Sri Lanka's five 
other bowlers used picked up at least a wicket as well. This was also incidentally the 
first time a team had gotten past the 40 overs or indeed the 200-mark against Sri Lanka 
this tournament. Will this be enough though to hand Sri Lanka their first loss of the 
tournament? Stay tuned as Shashwat will be with you shortly for the start of the chase.
